tools.name: propbank_lookup
tools.description:
Look up a lemma and every alternate of it in PropBank (at most 20 per call).

language is "en" or "zh". Returns Markdown: per lemma, every roleset with its roles and all
its examples (the sentence, then each argument; traces such as *T*-1 are PropBank's own),
or "not in PropBank". Lemmas over the limit are not looked up: the last line names them
(call again with them). There is no PropBank for another language (Uzbek): nothing.

messages.content:
## Input

Language: en
Document: en-0008, sentence 7 of 9

The previous sentences (at most five; number, tab, words):

2	Pope is the American businessman who was convicted last week on spying charges and sentenced to 20 years in a Russian prison .

3	He denied any wrongdoing .

4	Russian President Vladimir Putin pardoned him for health reasons .

5	Pope was flown to the U.S. military base at Ramstein , Germany .

6	He will spend the next several days at the medical center there before he returns home with his wife Sherry .

Their graphs:

# ::snt 2
# sentence level graph:
(s2i / identity-91
    :ARG1 (s2p / person
        :name (s2n / name :op1 "Pope"))
    :ARG2 (s2b / businessman
        :mod (s2c / country
            :wiki "United_States"
            :name (s2n2 / name :op1 "America"))
        :ARG1-of (s2a / and
            :op1 (s2c2 / convict-01
                :ARG1 s2b
                :ARG2 (s2c3 / charge-05
                    :ARG1 s2b
                    :ARG2 (s2s / spy-01
                        :ARG0 s2b
                        :aspect process)
                    :aspect performance)
                :temporal (s2w / week
                    :mod (s2l / last))
                :aspect performance)
            :op2 (s2s2 / sentence-01
                :ARG1 s2b
                :ARG2 (s2p2 / prison
                    :mod (s2c4 / country
                        :wiki "Russia"
                        :name (s2n3 / name :op1 "Russia")))
                :ARG4 (s2t / temporal-quantity
                    :quant 20
                    :unit (s2y / year))
                :aspect performance)))
    :aspect state)

# ::snt 3
# sentence level graph:
(s3d / deny-01
    :ARG0 (s3p / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG1 (s3d2 / do-02
        :ARG0 s3p
        :ARG1 (s3t / thing
            :mod (s3a / any)
            :ARG1-of (s3w / wrong-02))
        :aspect process)
    :aspect performance)

# ::snt 4
# sentence level graph:
(s4p / pardon-01
    :ARG0 (s4p2 / person
        :wiki "Vladimir_Putin"
        :name (s4n / name :op1 "Vladimir" :op2 "Putin")
        :ARG1-of (s4h2 / have-org-role-92
            :ARG2 (s4c / country
                :wiki "Russia"
                :name (s4n2 / name :op1 "Russia"))
            :ARG3 (s4p3 / president)))
    :ARG1 (s4p4 / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :cause (s4r / reason
        :mod (s4h / health))
    :aspect performance)

My choices, briefly:
- **Predicate:** I used `pardon-01` ("legally relieve of guilt"). Putin is the pardoner (`:ARG0`) and "him" is the guilty party (`:ARG1`). The other sense, `pardon-02`, is for forgiving a small social slip, so it doesn't fit here.
- **Putin's title:** "Russian President" is written as a role with `have-org-role-92`, with Russia as the organization (`:ARG2`) and `president` as the title (`:ARG3`). This follows the guidelines' "president of Russia" example.
- **"for health reasons":** This is a cause, so I wrote `:cause (reason :mod health)`. This is a judgment call. AMR often writes it as just `:cause (health)`, and the expert annotation may do the same.
- **Aspect:** `performance`, because the pardon is a finished event in the past.
- **"him":** Written as a third-person singular `person`. Linking him to the person he refers to in an earlier sentence happens later, in the document-level step.

# ::snt 5
# sentence level graph:
(s5f / fly-01
    :ARG1 (s5p / person
        :name (s5n / name :op1 "Pope"))
    :goal (s5b / base
        :mod (s5m / military)
        :possessor (s5c / country
            :wiki "United_States"
            :name (s5n2 / name :op1 "U.S."))
        :place (s5c2 / city

            :name (s5n3 / name :op1 "Ramstein")
            :place (s5c3 / country
                :wiki "Germany"
                :name (s5n4 / name :op1 "Germany"))))
    :aspect performance)

# ::snt 6
# sentence level graph:
(s6s / spend-02
    :ARG0 (s6p / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG1 (s6t / temporal-quantity
        :quant (s6s2 / several)
        :unit (s6d / day)
        :mod (s6n / next))
    :place (s6c / center
        :mod (s6m / medicine)
        :place (s6t2 / there))
    :temporal (s6b / before
        :op1 (s6r / return-01
            :ARG1 s6p
            :ARG4 (s6h / home)
            :companion (s6p2 / person
                :name (s6n2 / name :op1 "Sherry")
                :ARG1-of (s6h2 / have-rel-role-92
                    :ARG2 s6p
                    :ARG3 (s6w / wife)
                    :aspect state))
            :aspect performance))
    :aspect performance)

This sentence:

7	Pope was in remission from a rare form of bone cancer when he was arrested in Russia.

Its graph:

# ::snt 7
# sentence level graph:
(s7r / remission-02
    :ARG1 (s7f / form
        :mod (s7r2 / rare)
        :mod (s7c / cancer
            :mod (s7b / bone))
        :possessor (s7p / person
            :wiki "Edmond_Pope"
            :name (s7n / name :op1 "Pope")))
    :temporal (s7a / arrest-01
        :ARG1 s7p
        :place (s7c2 / country
            :wiki "Russia"
            :name (s7n2 / name :op1 "Russia"))
        :aspect performance)
    :aspect state)

content.text:
# document level relations:
(d / document
    :temporal ((document-creation-time :before s7a)
               (s7a :overlap s7r))
    :modal ((root :modal author)
            (author :full-affirmative s7r)
            (author :full-affirmative s7a))
    :coref ((s6p :same-entity s7p)
            (s4c :same-entity s7c2)))

My choices, briefly:
- **Time:** The arrest is a finished past event with no date in its clause, so its parent is `document-creation-time` (`:before`). The remission is a state that holds at the time of the arrest ("when he was arrested"), so it overlaps the arrest. I left out an order between the arrest and the conviction in sentence 2, because the text never states it directly.
- **Certainty:** The author states both events as plain facts, so each gets `full-affirmative` from the author.
- **Same entity:** Pope is linked to his closest earlier mention, "He" in sentence 6 (`s6p`). Russia is linked to its closest earlier mention as a whole country, `s4c` in sentence 4. The Russia in sentence 2 (`s2c4`) only describes the prison, so I didn't use it.
- **Lookups:** I didn't look anything up. Neither event's type or conceiver was in doubt.
